claim_one_line: THE THREAD'S OWN LINES (P-312, P-336; no data): a thread A fixes a flat line of exact order N up to sign iff N divides the larger Smith invariant of A - I or A + I (coker(A -+ I) = Z/d1 + Z/d2; 0 mismatches in 6 989 brute-force checks over 241 classes and N <= 30); the trace rule N | t -+ 2 is its squarefree case (153 failures, all at non-squarefree N), exact on orders 5 and 10; when the 5-torsion is cyclic the fixed order-5 lines are exactly +-v, +-2v (99/99), and multiplication by 2 commutes with A, so no thread-built rule chooses (the deck involution of X_1(5) -> X_0(5)); the mapping torus's orientation-reversing symmetries (e det g = -1) swap v <-> 2v (28/28) and preserving ones fix the pair (188/188); the frame is mirror-covariant (1e-11), so a reversing symmetry relates (P, v) to (gP, 2v) -- glides (g^2 = A on the tick) have no fixed point, half-turns fix a point Q that reduces to tau = i, where v and 2v agree to 4e-14 -- while at B1720's apexes they differ by 4.7-8.7 in log. So the bit is real wherever the frame has a hierarchy: a thread fixes tau and its line up to one bit, which a sealed test must declare or count. 0 of 19.
weave_or_thread: weave (a property of every thread and line)
